title: Skill-weighted Swap Market for Cycle Balancing and Emergency De-risking
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and pilot a lightweight ‘Skill-weighted Swap Market’ that lets teams trade partial staffing commitments across concurrent cycles. The market assigns a weight to each skill (frontend, infra, runtime, ML infra, SRE) based on scarcity and critical-path impact, and uses those weights to price swaps. The goal is to reduce mid-cycle derailment risk by enabling predictable, auditable short-term reassignments and compensatory credits while preserving ownership of high-risk deliverables.
acceptance_criteria: Pilot run with 3 cross-functional teams during 2026-W12 with documented swaps and zero unapproved scope loss

Swap ledger implemented in lightweight Google Sheet + audit webhook to Confluence; all swaps include: origin team, receiving team, skill tags, estimated points traded, weighted credit assigned, and expected rebalancing window
Post-pilot survey showing >=75% perceived fairness from participating PMs/EMs
Operational playbook (how-to, approvals, escalation) merged to Confluence and linked from cycle planning template
A runbook for emergency reverse-swap (fast rollback) and SLAs for decision latency published
proposed_workflow: 1) Teams flag request during weekly cadence-planning; supply: skill, hours/points, earliest release impact
2) Product Ops posts request to swap board with auto-calculated weight and suggested credit
3) Receiving team negotiates within 48 hours; PMs/EMs sign off; swap entered in ledger
4) Credits are tracked as fractional commitments to be repaid within two cycles or compensated via backlog credit
5) Quarterly reconciliation to adjust skill weights based on realized blocking incidents and staffing supply
risks: Gaming the weights: teams might misclassify work to receive favorable credits
Hidden technical debt: frequent swaps could surface unowned long-running maintenance work
Approval latency: slow sign-offs could negate benefit for critical-path interrupts
Measurement noise: subjective fairness vs. objective throughput may diverge; needs careful telemetry
stakeholders: Eng managers: Luca Moreno, Priya Sethi
